title: Patience and prayer are the two things to lean on.
subtitle: Where to take your strain

picture.label: Every day is one of two

then: Right after commanding gratitude, Allah commands patience and prayer. Ibn Kathir says a servant is always {reward}enjoying a blessing to thank for{/reward} or {trap}facing a hardship to bear patiently.{/trap} He cites the hadith: amazing is the believer, for whatever Allah decrees is good for him.
now: The rent is late, the boss sent a sharp email, the child has a fever again. You reach for your phone to vent. {idea}The verse points to two other tools: hold steady, and stand up to pray.{/idea} Then it adds the part that changes everything: Allah is with the patient.
old: When things go wrong, I have to handle it on my own.
new: Patience and prayer are where I draw strength, and Allah is with me in it.
try: Next time stress spikes, pray two rak'ahs before you message anyone about it.

title: Do not call them dead. They are alive.
subtitle: What we cannot perceive is still real

picture.label: What you see vs what is

then: Placed between commands to be patient, this verse speaks of those killed in the way of Allah. Ibn Kathir says {reward}they are alive and receiving provision{/reward}, and that a hadith speaks of the believer's soul in Paradise too, so naming martyrs is {idea}to honor them.{/idea}
now: Sitting with a family after a funeral, everyone speaks in past tense. The verse does not deny the grief. {idea}It widens the picture beyond what your eyes can reach.{/idea} What you cannot perceive is not the same as what is not there.
old: When someone dies for good, that is the end of their story.
new: Death ends what I can see, not what Allah gives.
try: Make dua today for a believer you lost, speaking of them with hope.

title: You will be tested with something of loss.
subtitle: The test is announced ahead of time
then: Allah tells the believers plainly that tests will come. Ibn Kathir notes the word {idea}something of{/idea}, meaning a little of each: some fear, some hunger, some wealth lost, loved ones dying, farms not giving what was expected. The verse ends with {reward}give good news to the patient.{/reward}
now: The layoff email. The harvest of your hard work smaller than planned. A phone call from the hospital. It feels like the floor gave way. {idea}The verse said it would come, long before it did.{/idea} You are not off the path. You are on the part of it that was announced.
old: If I am losing things, Allah must be displeased with me.
new: Loss was promised as a test, and the patient were promised good news.
try: Write down one loss this year and one thing it taught you.

title: We belong to Allah, and to Him we return.
subtitle: The words that reframe every loss
then: This is how Allah describes the patient. Ibn Kathir says they say it {idea}to comfort themselves{/idea}, knowing they belong to Allah and that nothing is lost with Him. Umm Salamah said these words with a dua when Abu Salamah died, and {reward}Allah gave her better: the Prophet ﷺ.{/reward}
now: The phone screen cracks. The sale falls through. The call comes that your uncle has passed. {idea}Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.{/idea} It is not a phrase only for funerals. It reminds you, in every size of loss, whose it all was.
old: What I lose was mine and it was taken from me.
new: Everything, including me, belongs to Allah and returns to Him.
try: Next small loss, even a dropped cup, say the words and ask Allah for something better.

title: Blessings, mercy, and guidance for the patient.
subtitle: What patience earns
then: After the patient say their words of return, Allah names their reward. {reward}'Umar bin Al-Khattab said: what righteous things, and what great heights.{/reward} He counted blessings and mercy as two good things, and {idea}being guided{/idea} as the heights above them.
now: You held it together at the hospital. You did not lash out after the bad news. Nobody clapped. {reward}The verse says your Lord sent blessings and mercy on you for it{/reward}, and called you guided.
new: Patience is met with blessings, mercy, and guidance from my Lord.
try: Remind someone going through a hard time of this verse in one gentle message.

title: Safa and Marwah: a mother's search became a symbol.
subtitle: Old hesitation cleared, and a lesson in need
then: 'A'ishah explained that some of the Ansar, who had once worshipped the idol Manat, {trap}hesitated to walk between Safa and Marwah{/trap} after Islam. The verse says these hills are {idea}among the symbols of Allah.{/idea} Ibn Kathir traces the walk to Hajar, going back and forth in fear and humility until Allah answered her with Zamzam.
now: You are pacing the corridor outside the delivery room, or walking laps around the kitchen at 2 a.m. worrying about money. {idea}Hajar walked like that too, with nothing but her need for Allah.{/idea} {reward}Allah calls even small good done willingly appreciated.{/reward}
old: My anxious pacing and begging are a sign of weak faith.
new: Running to Allah in need is so honored that He made it a symbol.
try: In your next worried moment, turn the pacing into a dua like Hajar's.

title: Hiding clear guidance is a heavy wrong.
subtitle: What happens when knowledge is buried

row.title: one who shares
sub: even fish seek forgiveness for him

then: Abu Al-'Aliyah said these verses came about {trap}People of the Scripture who hid the description of the Prophet ﷺ.{/trap} Ibn Kathir contrasts it: everything asks forgiveness for the one who teaches. Abu Hurayrah said that {idea}if not for this verse, he would not have narrated a hadith.{/idea}
now: You know how to fill out the form your new neighbour is struggling with. You know a short dua that would comfort your friend. You hold it back because it feels awkward. {idea}Knowledge that helps is meant to be passed on.{/idea}
old: What I know is mine to keep or share as I like.
new: Beneficial knowledge given to me is a trust meant for others.
try: Share one useful thing you know with someone who needs it today.

title: The door stays open: repent, repair, reveal.
subtitle: Three steps back from concealment
then: Right after the warning comes the exception. Ibn Kathir says it covers those who {idea}regret, correct their behavior, and explain what they had hidden.{/idea} He adds that even those who once called to innovation or disbelief, {reward}if they repent, Allah will forgive them.{/reward}
now: You told a half-truth at work and the project went the wrong way because of it. Or you kept quiet in a family dispute and someone took the blame. {reward}It is not too late.{/reward} {idea}Admit it, put it right, say what you held back.{/idea}
old: Once I have hidden something this long, I can never undo it.
new: Allah accepts the one who regrets, repairs, and brings the truth out.
try: Correct one small thing you left misleading, even with a short message.

title: The ending decides everything.
subtitle: Disbelief carried all the way to death
then: After opening the door of repentance, Allah describes those who {trap}disbelieve and die while still disbelieving.{/trap} The difference from the previous verse is {idea}the ending.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes some scholars avoided cursing a specific person {idea}because we do not know how Allah will make his end.{/idea}
now: You look at someone at work or in the family and write them off. Or you write yourself off after a bad year. {idea}No one's story is finished until it is finished.{/idea} The only ending you can work on is your own.
old: I already know how this person will end up.
new: Endings belong to Allah. My job is to keep turning back while I still can.
try: Ask Allah tonight for a good ending, for yourself and for someone you had given up on.

title: No lightening and no delay once it is too late.
subtitle: Why the time to turn is now
then: The verse describes those who died in disbelief: {trap}their punishment will not be lightened nor will they be given time.{/trap} Ibn Kathir ends this passage with a plea: {idea}we seek refuge with Allah from this evil end.{/idea}
now: The reminder on your phone says "start praying regularly." You snooze it again. Next month, after the exams, after the wedding. {idea}Every day you wake up is a reprieve given to you.{/idea} The verse is a warning, but it is also an open window.
old: There will always be time to fix things with Allah later.
new: This life is the time that was given. There is no delay after it.
try: Do today one act of return you have been postponing, however small.

title: One God, and He is Mercy itself.
subtitle: The center that everything else turns around
then: After warnings about concealment and disbelief, Allah states the core: {idea}your God is One God.{/idea} Then He names Himself {reward}the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.{/reward} Ibn Kathir reports a hadith that Allah's Greatest Name is in this verse and in the opening of Al-'Imran.
now: Your life has many pulls: the boss, the bank, the family's expectations, the feed. Each feels like it needs to be obeyed. {idea}There is only One worth that.{/idea} And the first thing He tells you about Himself, after His oneness, is mercy.
old: I have to keep everyone and everything pleased.
new: There is One I answer to, and He describes Himself first by mercy.
try: Recite this verse slowly once today, and name one thing you have treated like a master.

title: Sky, sea, rain, wind: signs for those who think.
subtitle: Proof of oneness in the ordinary
then: Right after declaring He is One, Allah lists the proofs. Ibn Kathir describes each: night and day following each other {idea}without delay for an instant{/idea}, ships carrying goods between lands, rain bringing dead earth to life, winds that bring mercy. {reward}All of it testifies to His oneness.{/reward}
now: Your delivery arrives from another continent. The rain hits the window on your commute. The days are getting shorter. You see it all and notice none of it. {idea}The verse asks you to look again, and think.{/idea}
old: Nature is just the background of my busy life.
new: The ordinary world is full of signs, if I stop and reason.
try: Next time it rains or the sun sets, put the phone down and look for one full minute.

title: Believers love Allah more than anything else.
subtitle: When love is given to rivals
then: Ibn Mas'ud asked the Prophet ﷺ about the greatest sin. He said: {trap}to set up a rival to Allah while He alone created you.{/trap} The believers are different: {reward}they love Allah more{/reward}, revere Him, and depend on Him for every need.
now: Not a statue. Maybe a career, a person, a team, a follower count. The thing you check first in the morning and think about last at night. {idea}Ask what holds the place in your heart that belongs to Allah.{/idea}
old: I love Allah, I just also live for other things.
new: Love for Allah is meant to be stronger than any other love I carry.
try: Notice the first thing you reach for on waking tomorrow. Make it remembrance of Allah instead.

title: The ones you followed will walk away from you.
subtitle: Every tie cut on the Day
then: The verse shows the moment when {trap}those who were followed declare themselves innocent of their followers.{/trap} Ibn Kathir cites Ibrahim telling his people their bond was only for this world, and on the Day {trap}you shall disown each other.{/trap}
now: You follow a person online so closely you take their opinions as your own. Or you go along with your friends because "everyone does it." {idea}Ask: will they stand with me when I answer for it?{/idea}
old: If I am following the crowd or a leader, the blame is on them.
new: Those I follow cannot carry me. I answer for whom I chose to follow.
try: Unfollow or mute one voice that pulls you away from what you know is right.

title: If only we had one more chance.
subtitle: Regret that comes after the door closes
then: The followers who were disowned wish to {trap}return to the world once more{/trap} so they could disown their leaders in turn. Instead, {trap}Allah shows them their deeds as regrets.{/trap} Ibn Kathir notes that if they had known what they would face, they would have left the path they lived by.
now: You are, right now, living the chance those people begged for. The same feed, the same friends, the same choices are in front of you today. {idea}Their wish is your ordinary Tuesday.{/idea}
old: I will change my direction when I am sure it matters.
new: The one more chance others will beg for is the day I am living now.
try: Choose one deed today you would want to see, not regret, on the Day.
